_README: PRE-REGISTERED CONFIRMATORY TEST FAMILIES for the language paper.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The analysis that decides a claim must be fixed before
the data that decides it exists, or the choice of test is a free parameter
fitted to the result. T-LX.18 commits this file BEFORE the five route-once
MoRE cells are trained, so the correction method, the family membership and
the primary metric cannot be reselected once the numbers land.
HOW IT IS CONSUMED. code/seed_stats.holm() takes `family_size` from the
`family_size` field below -- NOT from the number of tests that happened to
be computable. A declared comparison that could not be run still consumes a
slot. Dropping a failed arm must never make the survivors easier to call
significant.
HONEST DISCLOSURE, read this before citing the file as pre-registration.
This file is written at a point where the MoE and MoR arms are ALREADY
TRAINED and their numbers are known (MoE 3.9529 +/- 0.0396, MoR 3.5202 +/-
0.0406 on val/task_loss). Only the MoRE arm is being re-run. So:
- Every test whose `pre_result` is "unknown" is genuinely pre-registered.
- The single test marked "known" (mor_vs_moe) is NOT. It is declared here
anyway because it is read off the same table and must be corrected for;
omitting it to keep the family small would be the worse error. The paper
must state that this one comparison was specified after its data existed.
Do not describe the whole file as pre-registered. Describe it as it is.
frozen_by: T-LX.18 -- committed before the five route-once MoRE cells were trained; see changelog.md
correction_note: Holm-Bonferroni, not plain Bonferroni. Holm controls the same familywise
error rate and is uniformly more powerful, so the plain version is strictly
worse with no compensating property. This matters at the design's
resolution limit: the exact two-sided randomization test at 5 vs 5 has a
floor of 2/C(10,5) = 0.00794, so plain Bonferroni over 7 comparisons
(0.05/7 = 0.00714) would sit BELOW the floor and no effect of any size
could be declared significant. Holm's easiest threshold in a family of 4 is
0.05/4 = 0.0125, a margin of 0.0046 above the floor.
TWO FAMILIES, NOT ONE, and the reason must survive review. Family A asks
whether an architecture predicts better (metric: val/task_loss). Family B
asks whether recursion depth tracks per-token difficulty (metric:
depth/spearman_vs_model_loss). These are different hypotheses on different
quantities; pooling them would correct the depth claim for tests that cannot
bear on it. Splitting a family to buy power IS a degree of freedom, which is
why the split is declared here rather than chosen later -- and why no third
family may be added after results exist.

A_predictive_quality.metric_note: Final-epoch validation task loss, nats/token, lower is better. Per CLAUDE.md 4 this is the primary predictive metric; total_loss is never used for a verdict. best == last on all 15 published cells (log_interval = 1, monotone decrease), so no model selection occurred on this split.

tests.hypothesis: Recursion with routing predicts better than a single-pass sparse mixture at matched parameters.
Recursion alone predicts better than a single-pass sparse mixture at matched parameters.
tests.pre_result_note: gap +0.4327, p = 0.00794 (AT FLOOR). Declared after its data existed -- see _README.

tests.hypothesis: Adding expert routing on top of recursion predicts better than recursion alone.
tests.pre_result_note: The per-step MoRE arm gave +0.0172, p = 0.4048 -- a genuine null. If the route-once arm reproduces that null, Outcome B/C language is the honest reading and must be reported as such (CLAUDE.md 8).

tests.hypothesis: Adaptive halting predicts better than a FIXED depth equal to the adaptive arm's mean depth -- i.e. the benefit is adaptivity, not merely the average compute it spends.
tests.pre_result_note: This is the control that tests the paper's actual novelty claim. The fixed-depth path is already plumbed (model.py fixed_depth), so the arm is config-only. If it is not run, this slot stays N/A and still consumes a Holm slot; it must NOT be deleted to raise the other three thresholds.

B_adaptive_depth_mechanism.metric_note: Spearman rho between a token's allocated recursion depth and the model's own loss on that token -- the operational form of 'spends more compute where it is harder'. Reported per CLAUDE.md 4 as depth allocation behaviour, never as 'compute efficiency'.

tests.hypothesis: Routing once per token leaves depth allocation at least as difficulty-aligned as MoR's.
tests.pre_result_note: MoR measured +0.2953 +/- 0.0553. The per-step MoRE arm measured -0.0154 +/- 0.0186, i.e. no alignment at all; that is the defect the route-once fix addresses.

tests.hypothesis: Routing once per token, rather than re-routing at every recursion step, is necessary for depth to align with difficulty.
tests.pre_result_note: The per-step arm is the five already-published MoRE cells, kept unedited as a labelled ablation (CLAUDE.md 6). Their resolved_config.json must never be rewritten to add routing_persistence.

note: Everything below is EXPLORATORY and is reported with effect sizes and
intervals, UNCORRECTED and labelled as such. None of it may be promoted
into a confirmatory family after the fact, and none of it may carry a
significance verdict in the abstract or conclusions.
items: Fixed-depth sweep d = 1..6 as a descriptive curve (not a test per d).
Shuffled-depth control matched on the depth histogram.
Depth vs input mutual information on existing checkpoints.
Per-epoch gap trajectory: the MoRE-vs-MoE gap widens +0.379 -> +0.426 -> +0.450 across the 3-epoch budget.
Seed dispersion: MoRE +/- 0.0133 against MoE +/- 0.0396 and MoR +/- 0.0406.
Routing diagnostics: entropy H/log(E), Hungarian-matched accuracy, AMI, purity, cosine similarity mean and max.

FLOPs accounting: MoR/MoRE 4.14x, MoR/MoE 9.07x, MoRE/MoE 2.19x, against measured throughputs within 3% for MoR and MoRE (the workload is latency-bound, so the FLOP ratio is not a speedup -- CLAUDE.md 4).

prohibited: Reading a verdict off an uncorrected p-value when more than one comparison in a family is reported.
Reporting 'not significant' for a comparison whose min_p exceeds its Holm threshold -- that is undecidable and prints N/A.
Reducing family_size after results exist, by any route, including deleting an arm that was not run.
Adding a third confirmatory family, or moving an exploratory item into a confirmatory one.
Quoting 1/C(n_a+n_b, n_a) as the two-sided floor for equal arms. It is 2/C. See code/seed_stats.py.
